subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should session-memory sync pursue incremental chunk preservation on the current memory_index schema, rescue the open candidate PR, or intentionally keep full-entry reindex semantics with threshold/profiling mitigations?
rationale: The choice affects session-state correctness, overlap/chunk-boundary semantics, source-wide batching behavior, and whether the conflicting candidate branch is worth adopting.

options.title: Sponsor a fresh current-main fix
options.body: Implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and both direct and source-wide batching paths, with compaction and overlap coverage.

options.title: Rescue the open candidate PR
options.body: Ask an owner or contributor to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete or conflicting assumptions before review continues.

options.title: Reject incremental preservation
options.body: Keep full-entry reindex consistency and address the performance pain through thresholds, archival, or profiling-only work instead.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and both direct and source-wide batching paths, with compaction and overlap coverage.
